晉王 (the Prince of Jin) who defeated Helian Duo is not named here; kept as a title-only local person.
The English renders both 奚 and 霫 as 'Xi'; the packet gives no separate romanization for 霫, so no repair.
The division of the Tangut tribal and chief names (連香, 李八薩王, 悉那埋摩, 乞埋嵬悉逋) follows the packet's English; the tribe names are not surfaced as people.
每相溫 and 于越相溫 are kept as the packet romanizes them; 于越 may be a title, but the packet does not say so.
皇帝 (the Emperor) in the petitioners' words is linked to Emperor Wenzong, whose envoys they were addressing; the unit does not name him in the quotation.
至七年 (by the seventh year) names no era; it follows 晉天福五年, but left unresolved.
明年 (the following year) follows 天福七年 in s0112; left unresolved.
The relationships of Cao Yuanzhong, Cao Yuanshen and Yuangong to Cao Yijin are not stated; none asserted.
回鶻王仁喻 (Renyu, s0134) and 王仁裕 (Wang Renyu, s0148) are written with different characters; kept as separate local people.
The Fenghua Khan investiture in s0149 has no stated subject; linked to Wang Renyu from s0148 (strongly inferred).
天公主 (Heavenly Princess) and 媚祿都督 are generic styles for the khan's wife and chief minister; not linked to persons.
天子 (Son of Heaven) whose health was asked after is the reigning Jin emperor, not named in this chunk; kept as a title-only local person.
延年辟穀 means prolonging life and abstaining from grain; the English reads 延年 as a person 'Yan Nian'. Repairs proposed; no person created.
撚崖天子 (Nianya Son of Heaven) is the Tangut chieftain's style; 天子 here is part of his name, not a generic reference.
諲譔 (s0236) differs in its second character from 大諲撰 (s0234); linked to the same king, Yinzhuan, as the packet's English does.
傅能何華 is romanized Fu Nenghua in the packet, which omits 何; not repaired.
The idiomatic field uses Korean readings (Kim Jin), the literal field Chinese (Jin Zhen); not repaired.
昆明大鬼主, 羅殿王 and 普露靜王 are title-only rulers kept as local people.
真腦 is rendered Champa in both fields, but the unit describes Champa itself; the packet gives no romanization for 真腦, so not repaired.
猛火油 rendered Greek fire (idiomatic) and fierce fire oil (literal); left as translation choice.
